claims.claim: Epiphanius of Salamis was bishop of Salamis (also called Constantia), the metropolis of Cyprus.
Epiphanius lived approximately from c. 310–320 to 403 AD.
The work Homilia in laudes Mariae deiparae is classified as CPG 3771 and BHG 1143 in standard patristic catalogues.
The Clavis Patrum Graecorum classifies the work as spurious, and notes that it is also attributed to Hesychius of Jerusalem.
The work is dated to the 6th-8th century according to R. Caro, La Homiletica Mariana Griega.
The Greek text of the homily is preserved in Migne's Patrologia Graeca, volume 43, columns 485-501.
The work also survives in a Slavonic version with the incipit 'Сиꙗѭщиихъ зареи богородичьнныихъ лоучѧ'.
The homily is assigned to the liturgical date of December 26 in the Slavonic tradition.

The work contains a detailed physical description of the Virgin Mary, including that she was of middle stature, corn-coloured skin, blonde hair, with tawny and beautiful eyes, black-browed, with prominent nose, long-armed, long-fingered, and long-faced.
